_comment: Speeds keep a 30:20:18:35:22 ratio, scaled so a Scooter 20 sails Rome-Tunis in about 60 s. range_nm is the longest single leg the model can sail (Scooter 20: 1 min 30 s of sailing, Feeder 100: 2 min 40 s since it was sped up to 4.82 nm/s, Feedermax 200: 6 min, Trans Atlantic: Rome to New York, Dominator: 9,000 nm). max_owned is how many of each model the player can own. map_size (length, width in pixels) and map_color are how the ship is drawn on the map: container ships run yellow to red and gas tankers light green to dark blue (smallest to biggest), recovery boats brown (darker = bigger), icebreakers icebreaker red, tugs black. breakdown_factor scales the chance of a random breakdown (bigger ships are sturdier). fuel_tank is in fuel units; fuel_per_s is burned every second at sea, whatever the speed. Burn was set so fuel cost about a third of a leg's pay at full speed (about 40% since the fuel price rose 20%), and tanks are sized so a ship leaving at 100% maintenance can just finish a range_nm leg (plus 1 s spare) while wearing and slowing on the way. Icebreakers (icebreaker: diesel or nuclear) sail no routes either: they are stationed at an ice area and lead convoys through its seasonal ice (game_config icebreaking); they pay their own fuel and repairs. Recovery boats (recovery: true) sail no routes: they recover lost ships, and range_nm is the longest recovery job they can do. carries lists the models a recovery boat can carry (none listed = any). Tugs (tug: true) sail no routes either: they are based two to a port on your routes and push or drag lost ships within reach_nm of their port back in (game_config tugs); range_nm is how far one can sail to move to another port. The Mammoth costs the most to run; the Buffalo, the size of a Trans Atlantic, carries only Scooter 20s, Feeder 100s, Feedermax 200s and the Bunker, Lake and Coastal tankers and costs about a tenth as much to run. wear_pct_per_min is maintenance lost per minute of running at sea (the Dominator and Mammoth wear at half rate; speed is top speed x maintenance, so a ship at 0% stops); repair_cost_per_pct is set so repairs cost about 10% of what the ship earns sailing. dock_s is how long a ship unloads and loads at each port; repair, then refuel, each take refill_phase_s of that time. category groups the models in the shop: container ships, gas tankers and recovery boats. capacity is in the unit of the model's cargo (containers, tons, head, vehicles); cargo lists the commodities it can carry (data/markets.json). Each tanker size from the Coastal up is 10x the cargo and 15% slower than the last; the Bunker Tanker (tier 1, level 4) and Lake Tanker (tier 2, level 9) below it are priced and sized like the Laker and Grain Laker by cargo value. The new lines' fuel, tank and repair numbers follow the same rules as the old ones (fuel about 40% and repairs 10% of what a similar ship earned under the old flat pay, before both were halved). unlock_level is the company level needed to buy the model. seaway: true if the model fits the St. Lawrence Seaway and can sail to Great Lakes ports (Scooter 20, Feeder 100, Feedermax 200, Mini Bulker, Laker, Handysize, Grain Coaster, Grain Laker, Handymax, Stock Barge, Cattle Coaster, Stock Ship, Livestock Carrier, Bunker Tanker, Lake Tanker, Coastal, Car Barge, Short Sea Ro-Ro and Car Hopper, and both recovery boats so lake ships can be rescued). slot_every overrides game_config ship_slots' [start, every] every value for one model (the Scooter 20 and Feeder 100 get a slot every 2 levels). first_price, if set, is what the company pays for its first ever ship of that model (the Buffalo's first is $150,000); later ones cost price, and a ship sells for half what was paid for it. xp_first_level is the ship XP a ship needs for its first level; each level after costs 5% more (game_config ship_level_growth). Bigger models need disproportionately more, so small ships level fastest. min_port is the smallest port band the model can dock at (game_config port_sizes): tier-4 ships (Trans Atlantic and the other lines' middle ships) need Medium, tier-5 ships (Dominator and the other lines' biggest) need Large; smaller ships and recovery boats dock anywhere. Recovery boats earn XP by the mile on recovery jobs (game_config recovery_xp): a Buffalo job averages about 1,050 nm and a Mammoth one about 2,700 nm, so the first level takes about one job and level 30 about 20 hours of play. tier (1 to 5, from the smallest of a line to the biggest; service ships by their size) sets the captains and crew a model needs (game_config crew). Every cargo line has all five tiers (the fifteen added 2026-10-15 fill the gaps; see SPEC.md Ship models). art names the drawing a model uses when it is not its category's (the fishing and crabbing boats, the reefers and the fish tender). new_tier marks those fifteen: they are left out of the level costs of companies from before company types (Progression), so those keep their levels. The Fresh produce carriers (model_61 to model_65, category produce, farm_line: Agriculture's third line, added with the farms 2026-10-15 and left out of the level costs, so companies keep their levels) carry the fresh crops in pallets, refrigerated: fresh cargo loses value by the day aboard (data/farms.json crops loses_a_day), keeps_fresh less of it on the bigger ones. The cruise ships (model_51 to model_60, categories cruise_ocean and cruise_expedition, the Cruises company type) sail round-trip voyages (Cruises; game_config cruises). A model marked coming_soon would be kept out of play (GameData.upcoming_models) and shown on a coming-soon Shop tab. capacity is their guests with a balanced cabin mix; cruise: {guests, deck_slots (amenity slots), ice (polar_light: the Antarctic stations and icebound Arctic ports in season; polar: the Arctic routes in their open season too; polar_long: a longer polar season), helipad}. Their crews are a captain and mates by tier plus one hand for every 3 guests (GameState.crew_of()). The car carriers carry the car makers' goods and the boat carriers (model_66 to model_70, category boat_carriers, boat_line: the Vehicles type's second line, added with the makers 2026-10-15 and left out of the level costs, so companies keep their levels) the boat makers' (data/manufacturers.json): capacity is deck slots, and a maker's vehicle takes its hold of them (a superyacht 60). The boat carriers match the car carriers tier for tier, about 5% slower, their tanks a little bigger to match; the three smallest fit the Seaway.
